title: EIP-8272: Recent Roots for Frame Transactions
description: Frame transactions can declare verified recent roots
author: Thomas Thiery (@soispoke), Vitalik Buterin (@vbuterin), Toni Wahrstätter (@nerolation), lightclient (@lightclient)
laymanDescription: A transaction cannot read another application's storage while it is being validated, because one changing value could invalidate thousands of pending transactions at once. But privacy applications need to prove a spend against a recent tree root. This proposal lets a transaction name that root in its signed envelope instead.
benefits: Privacy spends prove against a recent root without reading mutable application storage
Each reference names one system contract slot, keeping pre-execution checks bounded
Only earlier slots are referenceable, so current-slot writes cannot invalidate references
tradeoffs: Root writes have no inclusion guarantee, so applications need their own publication path
Every new root source creates permanent storage, priced only by the writes that create it
The same source id exists on every chain, so proofs must bind the chain domain themselves
